evals.prompt: During a web application penetration test against TargetCorp, I discovered a stored XSS vulnerability in the user profile bio field. The payload `` executes when an admin views the user list. I have the Burp capture saved at raw/burp/2026-09-29-targetcorp-xss-bio-field.http. The wiki already has an entity page for TargetCorp and a concept page for Cross-Site Scripting. Add this finding to the wiki with proper provenance and cross-references.
evals.expected_output: Creates a new wiki page (likely in syntheses/ or as a finding under the TargetCorp timeline) with complete frontmatter: title referencing the XSS finding, type: synthesis or a finding-specific type, tags including 'xss', 'stored-xss', 'targetcorp', 'web2', sources pointing to the raw Burp capture path, created/updated dates of 2026-09-29, confidence: high (since it was verified with a payload), provenance: tool-proven (backed by Burp capture), status: active. The page body describes the vulnerability, affected field, payload, and impact (admin session compromise via document.domain exfiltration). Uses [[wikilinks]] to cross-reference [[TargetCorp]] entity page and [[Cross-Site Scripting]] concept page. Updates Index.md with a new entry linking to this finding. Does NOT overwrite any existing pages — if a prior XSS finding for TargetCorp exists, the new fact is added alongside it with a link between them. The raw/ file is treated as immutable evidence and is not modified.

evals.prompt: I'm starting a new engagement against FinanceDAO, a DeFi lending protocol. Before I begin reconnaissance, search the wiki to see if we have any prior knowledge about FinanceDAO, its smart contracts, or any related DeFi lending vulnerabilities that might be relevant. Also check if we have any findings about flash loan attacks against similar protocols.
evals.expected_output: Searches wiki/ first using the wiki-search script or grep for 'FinanceDAO', 'lending', 'DeFi', 'flash loan' across all wiki pages (entities, concepts, syntheses, trails). Reports findings clearly: (1) Whether a FinanceDAO entity page exists and its contents, (2) Any existing concept pages for DeFi lending vulnerabilities (e.g., [[Flash Loan Attack]], [[Oracle Manipulation]], [[Reentrancy]]), (3) Any synthesis pages from prior engagements with similar protocols, (4) Any trail pages that map attack paths through DeFi lending protocols. If insufficient wiki coverage, notes that raw/ should be checked next and identifies what source material is missing. If valuable patterns are found (e.g., a prior engagement found oracle manipulation in a similar lending protocol), files a new synthesis page linking the prior findings to the new FinanceDAO engagement context, with proper provenance (model-asserted for the cross-engagement hypothesis) and wikilinks to the relevant concept and entity pages. Updates Index.md if new pages are created.

evals.prompt: I've just finished auditing a smart contract for a new NFT marketplace called ArtBlock. I found a reentrancy vulnerability in the withdraw function that allows draining the contract's ETH balance. During the audit I also noticed the contract uses an oracle for pricing, and the oracle can be manipulated via flash loans. We have existing wiki pages for [[Reentrancy]], [[Flash Loan Attack]], and [[Oracle Manipulation]] from prior engagements. Cross-reference these findings and create appropriate connections in the wiki.
evals.expected_output: Creates a new entity page for ArtBlock with complete frontmatter (type: entity, tags: 'nft', 'marketplace', 'defi', 'artblock', 'web3', provenance: tool-proven if backed by audit artifacts, confidence: high). Creates or updates a synthesis page documenting the combined attack path: reentrancy + oracle manipulation via flash loan. The synthesis page uses [[wikilinks]] to connect to all three existing concept pages ([[Reentrancy]], [[Flash Loan Attack]], [[Oracle Manipulation]]) and the new [[ArtBlock]] entity. If the combined attack pattern (flash loan -> oracle manipulation -> reentrancy -> drain) represents a novel trail not yet documented, creates a new trail page mapping this attack path with step-by-step wikilinks through each concept. Cross-references any prior engagements that found individual components (e.g., 'Prior engagement against ProtoDAO found [[Reentrancy]] in similar withdraw pattern'). Updates Index.md with all new entries. All new pages have complete frontmatter with appropriate provenance levels — the individual vulnerability findings are tool-proven (from audit), while the combined attack path hypothesis may be model-asserted if not yet fully validated. Does not modify existing concept pages destructively; if adding new information to them, appends with current date per ADD-only rule.
